_readme: LEADERSHIP — this file controls the Leadership page.
You do not need to touch any HTML.
TO ADD A BOARD MEMBER: copy one whole block between { and }, paste
it inside the square brackets below, and edit the values. Put a
comma after every block EXCEPT the last one. A stray comma after
the final block is the most common cause of a blank page.
ORDER MATTERS: members appear on the page in the order they are
listed here. To move someone up the page, move their block up.
AT HANDOVER: replace boardYear with the new academic year, then
replace each name, program, year, bio and photo. Keep the roles.
FIELD BY FIELD:
name     Full name as they wish it published.
role     Office held, e.g. 'President'. Shown above the name.
program  e.g. 'M.D.' or 'M.D./Ph.D.'
year     e.g. 'MS2'
bio      Two or three sentences. Plain text only, no HTML.
photo    Path to a picture, e.g. 'assets/img/board/jane-doe.jpg'.
LEAVE IT AS "" IF THERE IS NO PHOTO — the site will show
the person's initials in a circle instead. It will never
show a broken image.
email    Optional. Leave as "" to publish no address. Addresses
on a public page do get collected by spam senders, so
the default is to leave these empty and route enquiries
through the chapter address on the Contact page.
vacant   Add "vacant": true to advertise an unfilled post. When
set, name and photo are ignored.
PHOTO TIPS: square pictures work best (the site crops to a circle).
Around 400x400 pixels is plenty. Save as .jpg, keep it under about
300 KB, and use a lower-case filename with hyphens and no spaces.
Please ask each person before publishing their photograph.

advisor.name: Edwin S. Monuki, M.D., Ph.D.
advisor.program: Warren L. Bostick Professor and Chair, Department of Pathology
advisor.bio: Dr. Monuki is Chair of Pathology at the UC Irvine School of Medicine and Associate Director of the Medical Scientist Training Program, with a joint appointment in Developmental & Cell Biology. His laboratory studies the human choroid plexus — the tissue that produces cerebrospinal fluid and forms the blood-CSF barrier — using stem cell models to explore its potential for regenerative medicine, alongside work on forebrain development and neuropathology. He earned his M.D. and Ph.D. in Neurosciences at UC San Diego and brings long experience mentoring physician-scientist trainees to the chapter.
